derivation: The old M/R/F/C transition-congruence audit reports 806 failures on 4x4-k4 and 30 on 4x4-k3.
Every one of those 836 failures is a future-equivalent representation split with zero terminal disagreement.
The ambiguity-realizability audit reduces all 836 occurrences to 68 unique differing residual contexts.
All 68 contexts are player-0/opponent-owned residuals containing every current open cap; all are exact support-schedule infeasible.
For a 4x4 board, the fixed final board mover is f=(16-1) mod 2 = 1.
G deletes from player 0 every residual containing every current open cap.
Therefore G deletes every residual token responsible for the 836 old representation splits.
The later RFG complete-4x4 audits are transition-congruent, consistent with this exact bridge.
The XOR audit independently shows parent and child support, hence X_h and p, are constant across every one of the 836 failure fibers.

findings.statement: Hereditary G exactly covers the residual-difference family responsible for all 836 old M/R/F/C transition-congruence failures on 4x4-k4/k3.
The 836 ambiguity family is therefore explained by a missed hereditary final-mover deadness rule, not by a missing support/XOR coordinate.
The same evidence simultaneously falsifies XOR as an ambiguity resolver: X_h,p are identical across each failure fiber because complete support is identical.

scope: complete 4x4-k4 and 4x4-k3 old-normal-form ambiguity family only
nonclaim: This does not establish that every future representation ambiguity on larger boards is a G-type all-open-cap case.
